title.narrative: Water-Energy-Food (WEF) Nexus in the West Bank

description.narrative: 01003568 Water-Energy-Food (WEF) Nexus in the West Bank For WEF covering three outputs and approved by LPAC . for Norway fund is only emphasis for output 01 and 02 (Output1: Solar PV system is developed and operationalized including energy efficiency measures at the identified water facilities in the north and south of the West BankOutput 2: Resilience fund for wells’ sustainable operation established and operationalized) without covering output 03 ( Output 3: Solar powered WWTP developed and opertionalzied for increased irrigation for agriculture in the Jordan Valley) PAMA: 1003501:Gaza throughout 2025, aiming to restore and strengthen the essential functions of the health system amid unprecedented crisis conditions. Implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the project responds to the urgent needs of internally displaced people (IDPs) and the wider population by addressing critical gaps in medical equipment, infrastructure, consumables, and human resource capacity across multiple hospitals and clinics in the Gaza Strip. Its overarching goal is to reinforce the resilience of healthcare facilities so they can continue delivering safe, reliable, and life-saving services despite the continued impact of conflict and resource shortages.A major component of the project focuses on revitalizing renal care services, particularly at Nasser Medical Complex, where ten new hemodialysis machines and ten dialysis chairs were installed, with twenty additional machines scheduled to replace aging units across other hospitals. This intervention directly strengthens access to essential dialysis treatment for more than 500 patients living with chronic kidney disease, significantly improving comfort, continuity of care, and patient safety.The project also advances hospital functionality by upgrading medical furniture and cold-chain storage infrastructure at the European Gaza Hospital (EGH) and Al-Zawaidah Hospital.
